newsitem.title: UK: Dominion to run E. Mids as stand-alone unit.
newsitem.headline: Dominion to run E. Mids as stand-alone unit.

text.p: U.S. energy utility Dominion Resources Inc said on Wednesday it planned to run Britain's East Midlands Electricity Plc as a stand-alone business and was hopeful of regulatory approval for its bid.

Dominion chief financial officer Linwood Robertson told Reuters that its 1.3 billion pounds ($2.15 billion) cash offer, agreed on Tuesday evening with East Midlands, was at a full and fair price and said the group hoped to keep East Midlands' management team, which is highly regarded by industry analysts.

Robertson said Dominion representatives were now talking to the regulator. "We intend to run this as a stand-alone business," he said, adding that he certainly hoped for approval from British electricity regulator Offer.

"We are very impressed with Norman Askew and his team and very much hope to keep them," Robertson said of East Midlands' chief executive and management staff. East Midlands was the first of Britain's electricity utilities, which were privatised with strong cash balance sheets, to launch a share buy-back to redistribute cash to shareholders.
Robertson said Dominion met East Midlands at 1630 GMT on Tuesday and, although legal and other detailed discussions continued well into Wednesday, "the business people finished much earlier."

East Midlands had previously said it would reject any offer from the Virginia-based utility pitched at around 608 pence per share. But Robertson, commenting on the 670 pence per share agreed bid price, said Dominion had never formally indicated a price and he noted press comment which pitched East Midlands' value at between 650 and 700 pence per share. Robertson said Dominion looked forward to the diversification East Midlands would bring to it and said the U.S. company would bring strengths to the British firm. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
